steps.title: Points for progress
steps.body: Scoring rewards different kinds of success. Reaching the end zone is worth the most, but ==getting close== still earns something.

steps.title: Touchdown
steps.body: Carry the ball into the end zone, or ==catch it there== with both feet down. That's a ==touchdown==, worth 6 points.
steps.note: Ref signal: both arms straight up.

steps.title: The try
steps.body: After a touchdown the team gets one bonus snap. ==Kick it== through the uprights for 1 point, or ==run or pass== it in again for 2.

steps.title: Field goal
steps.body: When a drive stalls close enough, the team can ==kick it through the uprights== on any down for ==3 points==.

steps.title: Safety
steps.body: If the offense is tackled ==in its own end zone==, the defense scores a ==safety==: 2 points, and the defense's team gets the ball back on a kick.
steps.note: Ref signal: palms pressed together above the head.

steps.title: Do the math
steps.body: A touchdown plus a kick is 7, so a ==7-point lead== is called a one-score game. A ==3-point lead== can vanish on one field goal. Those numbers drive late-game choices.

steps.prompt: What did the defense just score?
steps.explain: The quarterback was tackled inside his own end zone. That's a safety: 2 points for the defense, and they get the ball back.

steps.prompt: How many points is a field goal worth?
steps.explain: A field goal is 3. A touchdown is 6, the kick after it is 1, and a safety is 2.
